newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury sees no earnings impact from bank.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury sees no earnings impact from bank.

text.p: British supermarket retailer J. Sainsbury Plc does not expect any earnings impact from its joint venture with Bank of Scotland Sainsbury's Bank this year, group communications director Dominic Fry said.
"Sainsbury's Bank is a separate entity...with its own bottom line, (so) we don't expect to see any impact for Sainsbury's...this year," he told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
Sainsbury's Bank was launched on Wednesday offering an Instant Access account with 5.75 percent annual gross interest along with Visa credit cards.
Points in Sainsbury's Reward loyalty scheme are being offered as incentives to persuade customers to use the services.
Sainsbury, which holds 55 percent in the bank while Bank of Scotland has 45 percent, announced plans for its start up in October 1996.
The bank gained a licence earlier this month.
Sainsbury is the first supermarket to launch a bank although rival Tesco has linked up with Royal Bank of Scotland and Safeway with Abbey National to offer financial services.
